items.summary: In professional life sciences workflows, scientists routinely interpret visual artifacts (gel blots, microscopy images, plasmid maps, flow cytometry plots, molecular structures, ...) to inform research decisions. items.summary: Scarce data and tumor heterogeneity limit patient-level cancer treatment-response prediction. items.summary: Contextualization is essential for production automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems, where user-provided phrases must be recognized accurately under strict latency constraints. items.summary: The rapid symptom change of Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) makes it critical to have time-sensitive prediction models. items.summary: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has demonstrated significant gains in image captioning, yet it is still limited in encouraging Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to explore novel reasoning strategies. items.summary: Foundation models for medical image segmentation, like prompt-based MedSAM, generalize well across domains and modalities, often in zero or few-shot setups. items.title: Sparse Token Routing in Efficient Transformers
items.summary: Efficient-transformer research often motivates token pruning and adaptive computation with the claim that not all tokens require equal computational effort. We test this claim end to end using SEWN, a two-stream Transformer that routes tokens through either lightweight or full-capacity processing using a learned gate.
